what: Work cards are tiled endlessly as rounded glass panels (520×328, gap 26, corner .15, lens width .135, refraction .13 × card width) in a single shader (WebGL2). The whole sheet bulges at the center like a CRT (.22, more vertically on portrait screens), narrows toward the edges, and fades to dark at .15 on the sides and .18 top and bottom. Each panel’s edge lens pulls the image inward and pulls red, green and blue differently at .93, 1 and 1.08, forming a rainbow rim, and the light drifts slowly at rest and follows the hand. Drag and it follows, release and it glides on at ×.94 per frame (the wheel moves it directly, with .22 as inertia, after 90ms). The hovered panel grows 4% on a spring and turns ”on” over .65s, raising scanlines and contrast and glowing around it (.18s when moving, .3s when leaving). Mono cards show half through as an empty channel with noise, scanlines and a rolling band. On entry the cards appear from the center card outward (1.15s spread + .24s wobble), each starting at .6× and popping slightly at .72s. On press the whole-sheet scale grows logarithmically and that card flies over 1.15s (progress linear → cubic-bezier(.5,0,.12,1)) to the box (detail.box of fx:open, or a 16:9 with .15 top and .1 sides if absent), becoming a flat 16:9 panel (corner .035). The title text is erased until progress .55 and the remaining panels sink fully into the background by .85. Sending fx:close brings it back in .95s

options.[data-fx-part=card]: Card links (in order): data-title and data-sub (the card name and one-line text), data-label (what to put in when there is no photo), data-mono (empty monochrome channel), inside If present, it is fitted over that photo
options.card: Card base width (px), default 520 — on an endless board, below 640 screen width it is width × .86/520, above that width/1850 clamped to .52~.96, times 1.5 and multiplied by zoom. On a fixed-column board the width is fitted exactly to the column count.
options.zoom: Zoom of the endless board, default .72 (center card measured at 440px @1440 in the original)
options.scale: To fix the scale, you can
options.edge · edge-y: Fade width into darkness at the sides and top/bottom, default .15·.18
options.cols: Number of columns in the fixed grid board (0 for endless) — fits board height to the row count
options.wheel: window (default, scrolling anywhere on the page)·element·none
options.intro: Delay before entering starts (seconds), default 0 — if fx:start is sent, it starts then
options.focus · follow: When off, pressing does not make it fly in (only sends fx:open) / after flying in, it does not navigate to the link (only sends fx:opened)
options.fx:start · fx:open · fx:opened: Entry restart / pressed card (index · href) — the receiver is detail.box = {x,y,w,h}If given (screen px), it flies into that box / after it flies in and becomes a panel
options.fx:close · fx:closed: Return opened cards to the grid (.95s) / After all have returned

use:
Project One…
· Chosen cells: data-fx-crt-glass-lattice="cols: 2; wheel: none; drag: off"
note: Dragging is this part’s job, so touch on the board does not scroll the page (touch-action: none). The endless board is used only for a Hero that fills the screen. When placed between text, use a column board set with cols (drag: off, touch scrolls the page). The hand position is moved with the same formula as the board bulge to find the column, and the visible card is pressed. A similar endless shader grid is card-tunnel-grid (bends into a tunnel with speed) — that one is about glass lens, CRT and power-on effects. A board with dragging turned off (drag: off) also opens a card when released within 6px of where it was pressed
